verdicts.note: Faithful. 'Thy friend ... him ... his ear' is Othello himself. Just after 'I think Cassio's an honest man', a listener would take the third-person 'your friend' as Cassio. First person plus 'your friend — me —' fixes that, and the emphatic 'me' is natural in Othello's voice, not a footnote. 'Betraying' renders 'conspire against' (act treacherously toward) naturally. 'If you even think' = 'if thou but think'st', and the ear-as-stranger image is kept. Putting 'Iago' first avoids 'me, Iago'. Only the rhetorical third-person self-reference is traded, and that is for clarity. Conventions OK: spaced em dashes, straight apostrophes, no ellipses.

Faithful. Schmidt glosses 'conversation' in this very line as 'address, deportment' (Onions: 'behaviour, conduct'), so 'manners' corrects v1's false-friend 'ways of talking'. 'Smooth, charming' renders 'soft parts'. Onions glosses 'chamberer' as 'frequenter of ladies' chambers, gallant', so 'the ladies' men who frequent women's chambers' keeps the chamber image and removes the 'bedroom ladies' misparse. It also keeps the contrast with Othello the soldier (Schmidt: chamberer is 'opposed to a soldier'). 'Ladies'/women's' is mildly redundant, but it is clear by ear and woven into the sentence, not footnote-like. The line runs cleanly into 'into the valley of old age'. Conventions OK.

Not an invention. Percy (Furness) reads 'forked plague' as 'the horns of the cuckold'; Schmidt and Onions gloss 'forked' as horned or cuckolded. 'A betrayed husband' says 'cuckold' in plain words. Naming the forehead is justified: Furness endorses Rymer and Delius that Othello's 'pain upon my forehead' (9.105) alludes to the forked plague, and the listener needs the image to catch it. The appositive is concrete imagery in Othello's voice, not a dictionary aside. 'Even from the moment we're conceived' renders 'Even then ... when we do quicken' (Schmidt: quicken = 'to receive life'; Onions: 'to become living'). Attaching 'even' to conception restores the original's 'Even then'. 'Here comes Desdemona' = 'Desdemona comes'. Conventions OK.

Faithful, and it fixes the stated problem: restating 'they' before 'burn' stops the listener hearing 'the blood burn', and the semicolon clause is natural. Schmidt glosses 'distaste' as 'to be unsavoury', citing this very line, so 'barely taste unpleasant' is exact. 'Working a little on the blood' = 'with a little act upon the blood'. 'Sulfur' is the house US spelling, and 'Just as I said' = 'I did say so' (as Othello comes into view). 'Suspicions' (unchanged from v1) narrows 'conceits' (Schmidt: conception, idea), but the context supports it: the poison Iago has planted, and the 'horrible conceit' of III.3.115. The lowercase start follows the preceding unit's colon. Conventions OK.

Keeping v1 is right: 15.158 is identical to v1. Schmidt glosses 'naked' as '3) unarmed', citing 'naked as I am, I will assault thee' (Oth.), and Onions has 'unarmed' at Oth. V.ii.257. 'Unarmed' answers Gratiano's 'You have no weapon' directly and sets up 'Behold, I have a weapon'. 'Defenseless' would be looser. Natural by ear; conventions OK.

Confirmed. A word diff against v1 (candidate sha256 012ede1e…) shows the only change in 7.19 is 'endeavour' to 'endeavor'. The rest of the Clown's paragraph is identical. A rescan of the whole v2 finds no British -our spellings left.

Located at 11.105 (IAGO: 'give her a license to sin'; original 'give her patent to offend'). It is the only licence/license anywhere in v1 or v2. A word diff against v1 shows 'licence' to 'license' is the only change in the paragraph. 'License' is the correct US spelling for the noun.
